title: The Firefly Bridge
description: Mila and Pipo help a hedgehog cross a stream and learn when to step back and wait.

cover.alt: Mila, Pipo and a hedgehog beside a bark bridge lit by fireflies.

illustration.alt: Mila and Pipo walk among fireflies and find a hedgehog beside a stream with no bridge.

blocks.title: Lights along the path
lines: Mila was walking with her little dragon, Pipo, as the garden began to grow dark.
Fireflies glowed above the winding path like tiny floating lamps.
Pipo watched their lights flicker between the flowers.
Then something moving beside the stream caught Mila’s attention.

blocks.title: A missing bridge
lines: A hedgehog waited on the bank, staring at the path on the other side.
The rain had washed away the little bridge it normally used.
A few wet twigs were all that remained between the stones.
Mila decided to find a way to help the visitor continue its walk.

variants.prompt: Which animal is waiting beside the missing crossing?
variants.correctFeedback: Yes! A hedgehog is waiting beside the water.
variants.retryFeedback: Look for the little animal with prickles on its back.

variants.prompt: What event left the hedgehog without its usual crossing?

options.text: The rain washed the bridge away

variants.correctFeedback: That’s right: the rain carried the bridge away.
variants.retryFeedback: Read what the rain did, then look at the wet twigs.

illustration.alt: A leaf bends over the water and Pipo cannot move a heavy branch.

blocks.title: The leaf bends
lines: Mila picked up a leaf that looked wide enough to cover the gap.
She carefully stretched it between the banks, holding down its edges.
As soon as the middle touched the water, it began to fold.
The leaf was wide, but it was not firm enough for a bridge.

blocks.title: A heavy branch
lines: Pipo spotted a branch that seemed much stronger than the leaf.
He pushed with his front paws and planted his back feet firmly.
The branch barely moved, and the little dragon sat down beside it.
They had found something strong, but now it was too heavy to move.

variants.prompt: Which material is Pipo trying to move?
variants.correctFeedback: Yes! Pipo is trying to move a branch.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at what Pipo is pushing with his front paws.

variants.prompt: What did they discover by trying these two materials?

options.text: The leaf bent and the branch was too heavy

variants.correctFeedback: Exactly: they needed something firm that they could move.
variants.retryFeedback: Compare what happened to the leaf with Pipo’s effort to push the branch.

illustration.alt: Mila chooses bark and stones and builds a small crossing over the stream.

blocks.title: Bark and two stones
lines: Before trying another branch, Mila stopped to look around.
Under a tree, she discovered a wide, light piece of bark.
It felt firm, and she could easily lift it with both hands.
She chose two smooth stones to keep its ends out of the water.

blocks.title: A new bridge
lines: Mila set one stone near each bank of the narrow stream.
Then she rested the bark across them, leaving room for water underneath.
Pipo leaned closer to examine the shape of their new bridge.
This time, the material stayed straight across the gap.

variants.prompt: Which objects support the two ends of the crossing?
variants.correctFeedback: Yes! A stone holds up each end.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the grey objects underneath the bark.

variants.prompt: What job do the supporting stones do?

options.text: To hold the bark above the water

variants.correctFeedback: That’s right: the stones keep the bark above the water.
variants.retryFeedback: Look at the ends of the bark and the water flowing below.

illustration.alt: Mila tests the bridge with a pebble and notices the hedgehog hesitating at the entrance.

blocks.title: Testing the bridge
lines: Mila wanted to check whether the bark would hold steady.
She placed a small pebble in the middle and watched for any bending.
The bark supported the weight without sinking into the water.
She removed the pebble, leaving the little path clear.

blocks.title: The hedgehog waits
lines: The hedgehog took a few steps forward, but then it stopped again.
Pipo leaned toward it encouragingly, and the visitor tucked in its head.
Mila realized that a sturdy bridge was only part of the solution.
She and Pipo were standing too close and partly blocking the entrance.

variants.prompt: Which object did Mila place in the center during her test?
variants.correctFeedback: Yes! She tested it with a little pebble.
variants.retryFeedback: Look for the small grey object Mila places on the bark.

variants.prompt: What did Mila want to check before the hedgehog crossed?

options.text: That the bridge would stay steady
That Pipo could learn to swim
That the fireflies would stop glowing

variants.correctFeedback: Exactly: she wanted to see whether the bark would hold steady.
variants.retryFeedback: Read what Mila watched for when she put weight on the bridge.

illustration.alt: Mila and Pipo step back as fireflies glow and the hedgehog crosses the bridge.

blocks.title: Room to move
lines: Mila signaled to Pipo, and they both backed away slowly.
They waited quietly, allowing the hedgehog to choose when to move.
Fireflies shone above the bark and among the flowers along the bank.
At last, the little visitor had a clear path all the way across.

blocks.title: Across at last
lines: The hedgehog placed one paw on the bark and continued to the far bank.
Mila and Pipo watched it disappear among the flowers without following it.
They had chosen the right material and built a steady crossing.
They had also learned that helping sometimes meant stepping back and being patient.

variants.prompt: Which animal finally uses the new crossing?
variants.correctFeedback: Yes! The hedgehog can continue its walk.
variants.retryFeedback: Look for the little animal with prickles on the bridge.

variants.prompt: What else did the hedgehog need before it could move forward?
variants.correctFeedback: That’s right: giving it space and time was another way to help.
variants.retryFeedback: Compare where Mila and Pipo stood before and after they stepped back.

attention.example: She paid close attention while her dad showed her how to fix the bike.

normally.definition: In the way that usually happens.
normally.example: We normally walk to school, but today it was raining.

firmly.example: He held the ladder firmly while his sister climbed up.

discovered.definition: Found something that was not noticed before.
discovered.example: She discovered an old coin buried in the backyard.

examine.definition: Look closely at something to learn about it.
examine.example: The doctor examined the toy to see why it stopped working.

supported.definition: Held something up so it did not fall.
supported.example: Two thick branches supported the treehouse.

solution.definition: A way to solve a problem.
solution.example: Taping the box shut was a simple solution to keep it from opening.

entrance.definition: The place where you go into an area.
entrance.example: We waited by the entrance of the library until it opened.

patient.example: She was patient while her little brother tied his own shoes.
